title: Bechtle and IQM Awarded DLR QCI Contract to Supply Superconducting Cloud Resources - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Bechtle and IQM won a multi-year DLR QCI framework contract (through June 2027) to supply cloud access to IQM superconducting QPUs plus a dedicated classical server in IQM's Munich data center, with all workloads kept in Germany. It adds superconducting hardware to DLR QCI's ion-trap, neutral-atom, photonic and NV-center portfolio.

insights.claim: Bechtle and IQM (NASDAQ: IQMX) were awarded a public contract by the German Aerospace Center's Quantum Computing Initiative (DLR QCI) to supply cloud-based quantum computing resources and hybrid infrastructure under a multi-year framework agreement running through June 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Public-sector contract win gives IQM a visible revenue anchor and reference customer in Germany.
insights.locator: IT service provider Bechtle and superconducting

insights.claim: Bechtle will give DLR QCI teams managed access to IQM's production-grade superconducting processors via the IQM Resonance cloud platform.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Resale of QPU access through an IT integrator is a channel model to watch for quantum hardware vendors.

insights.claim: The award builds on the commercial partnership Bechtle and IQM established in 2024.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows a two-year partnership converting into a public contract.
insights.locator: The award expands upon the commercial partnership

insights.claim: DLR QCI's existing hardware portfolio already includes ion-trap, neutral-atom, photonic and NV-center systems, and the contract adds European-built superconducting hardware for application benchmarking in materials science, aerospace engineering, mobility and security.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Government buyers are hedging across qubit modalities rather than picking one winner.

insights.claim: The contract includes a dedicated classical server placed alongside IQM's quantum hardware at its Munich data center to support hybrid quantum-classical and HPC workflows.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Co-located classical compute is becoming a standard part of QPU deals.

insights.claim: Bechtle's IT System House Bonn will set up platform governance, account management and operational user support for DLR QCI researchers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Integrators capture services revenue around QPU access.

insights.claim: The agreement reinforces national data sovereignty requirements for Germany's federally funded research programs under the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, with all quantum and classical workloads hosted and processed in Germany.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
entities: Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space
insights.so_what: Sovereignty requirements favor European-built hardware and in-country hosting in public tenders.
insights.locator: The award expands upon the commercial partnership
